content.title: How Manchester City beat Arsenal to close gap at Premier League summit to three points
content.text: Manchester City close the gap on ArsenalManchester City have cut Arsenal’s lead at the top of the Premier League down to three points.Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland got the goals for the hosts, either side of Kai Havertz’s equaliser, in a massive victory.Gabriel was fortunate to avoid a red card after leaning into Haaland as the pair went head to head in the closing stages, but was unable to affect the result.Having stolen the ball of Gianluigi Donnarumma’s toes for Arsenal’s equaliser, Havertz missed a couple of golden opportunities for the visitors, including a free header deep into stoppage time.City travel to Burnley on Wednesday for their game in hand knowing that victory will take them top of the table.Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementManchester City and Arsenal's remaining fixtures Getty ImagesManchester City have six left to play while Arsenal have five. These are the fixtures standing between the Premier League's top two before the trophy is handed out.Manchester City's remaining PL fixturesApril 22: Burnley vs Manchester CityMay 4: Everton vs Manchester CityMay 9: Manchester City vs BrentfordMay 17: Bournemouth vs Manchester CityMay 22: Manchester City vs Crystal Palace (set to be moved)May 24: Manchester City vs Aston VillaArsenal's remaining PL fixturesApril 25: Arsenal vs NewcastleMay 2: Arsenalvs FulhamMay 10: West Ham vs ArsenalMay 17: Arsenal vs BurnleyMay 24: Crystal Palace vs ArsenalA reminder that Manchester City are in the semi-finals of the FA Cup while Arsenal are in the semi-finals of the Champions League.Manchester City ready to pounce Premier LeagueArsenal's dominance of top spot in the Premier League this season looks set to be broken on Wednesday.Victory over Burnley will take Manchester City above Mikel Arteta's men and that will surely make them favourites to lift the trophy in a few weeks' time.Below them, there is a battle bubbling away for the European places but Aston Villa and Liverpool's wins today have strengthened their grip on a place in next season's Champions League.What next for Manchester City? Getty ImagesAs for City, their next Premier League match arrives quickly with the trip to face Burnley on Wednesday.They will go top of the table with a victory there and will be keen to boost their goal difference.What next for Arsenal? Getty ImagesMikel Arteta's side are next in action in the Premier League against Newcastle United on Saturday, April 25. They then take on Atletico Madrid in the first leg of their Champions League semi-final on Wednesday, April 29.Arteta happy with Arsenal's level This result is a blow for Arsenal, make no mistake. But Mikel Arteta is happy with what he saw from his team today, as he told Sky Sports:💬 “We are at the level we are in because this team has taken us there. Today there were certain elements in front of goal where we missed key chances and could not come away with three points. It was a real battle as well with intensity and you expect that. “We take it game by game. We had some very big moments a few days ago in the Champions League as well. We are the only team that is playing and playing. We have seen the level today, we can cope with that and play even better.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement'It's not done' The message from Declan Rice — picked up on the cameras as full time at the Etihad — is clear. “It's not done,” said the Arsenal midfielder and fans will certainly hope so.Let's hear from Mikel ArtetaThe Arsenal manager still has belief in his team in this title fight — here's what he had to say when speaking to Sky Sports:💬 “When you don’t do it (score) and they have individual quality to deliver the moments that they have then that’s the difference in losing the game because I don’t think there is much between the two teams.“There is an element of luck if the ball goes in or not. There is the quality as well to be cool, precise and do this.“The way we ended the game, right from the beginning in the attitude of the team (was good). We could have had more quality in certain moments but we have been very close, not close enough. We have to reset, we had an opportunity today, a big one but there are five games to go.”Sky Sports apologises after Erling Haaland calls Bernardo Silva ‘F—ing Cannavaro’ UK broadcaster Sky Sports was forced to apologise after Erling Haaland called Bernardo Silva ‘f—ing Cannavaro’ following Manchester City’s 2-1 win against Arsenal. The pair were interviewed after the match, with Haaland having scored the winning goal and Bernardo winning Sky’s player of the match award. It was an all-action performance from the Portuguese midfielder, who is leaving City at the end of the season, and one moment from the victory at the Etihad Stadium was picked out. Late in the game, the 5ft 8in (173cm) Silva rose highest in the penalty area to head clear a dangerous delivery, which drew high praise from the 6ft 4ins (194cm) Haaland.Guardiola pays tribute to brilliant Bernardo Getty ImagesThere was almost an emotional moment in Pep Guardiola's post-match interview with Sky Sports when he was asked about Bernardo Silva, who is leaving the club at the end of the season.💬 “If you continue to talk, I will cry so be careful. We will be so emotional the moment he leaves. Bernardo is Bernardo, you cannot define him. Thank you Gary (Neville) for the Man of the Match — good decision.“He is not always seen by the public; he’s not fast, he’s not strong. But football starts from here (the head) and finishes with the feet. And this guy has got it here (his head). I’m just grateful. I feel gratitude for what these guys have done for many, many years.”Game on in the title raceWell, what a game. The full-time scenes were wild here inside the Etihad Stadium: Donnarumma jumped into the stands behind his goal due to what must be an incredibly complicated mixture of emotions, and was then hugged by his team-mates when he made his way back to the pitch — not least by Erling Haaland, who grabbed him and lifted him off his feet. Arsenal will probably feel they had the chances, or at least went close enough, to have won the match. But City’s spirit and Haaland’s patience in his battle with the Gunners defenders was enough to land a major, major result. Game on!SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementArsenal keeping City's seat warm? The AthleticIn total, including 206 days so far this season, Arsenal have led the Premier League for 1,518 days under Arteta. Over the same period, City have led for 1,201 days, yet the title count reads four to them and none to Arsenal.Let's hear from Pep Guardiola Getty ImagesThe City manager has been speaking to Sky Sports after that result, here's what he had to say:💬 “They are one of the most competitive teams I have faced in my career in terms of duels and one against ones. In second balls they are fantastic, with Rice and Havertz. We had momentum, they had momentum and in the end we escaped with a win. “Both teams have really top managers and top players. They are top of hte league with one goal difference, we will enjoy it and celebrate it and take the good things. But we have to focus and the focus in three days is going to Burnley. “I’m happy because we can extend the hope.”Get briefed on Manchester City 2-1 ArsenalMissed the match?Want to know how City won the tactical battle? Well, good news — you can dive into a fresh edition of The Briefing, where our writers break down all the biggest talking points, on the link below.Exactly what Arsenal are still missing Once again, we’re at the end of the season wondering what would have been if Arsenal had a clinical striker in their team.Kai Havertz deserves tremendous credit for the first-half equaliser but the frontman of a title-chasing side cannot afford to miss those two massive second-half chances.By contrast, Erling Haaland scrapped and battled away against two of the world’s leading centre-backs and scored the winning goal while holding Gabriel at arm’s length.Where would Arsenal be if they had a striker like Haaland in their squad? Home and hosed, I reckon.Are there positives to take for Arsenal?If the response from some Arsenal fans is anything to go by then, yes!Opinion might be split between doom-and-gloom and a more balanced reflection on what was a decent Arsenal performance despite the result. You can see how fellow fans feel about that result in the discussion tab above.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementA tough one to take Getty ImagesMikel Arteta is no stranger to the feeling of the Premier League title slipping through his fingers.His players still have the advantage but he knows that Manchester City are likely to be top of the Premier League table next time Arsenal play.A bitter pill to swallow.Odegaard still believesSpeaking to Sky Sports, Martin Odegaard was also asked about the increasing volume of noise surrounding Arsenal’s inability to hang onto their lead at the Premier League summit …💬 “There’s always that in football: pressure and noise. That’s a part of being a football player at this level. It’s completely normal to us.“We’ve just got to keep going, stay focused on ourselves, like we have done all season, and look forward to the next game. Bounce back, get a win there and move on — that’s all we’re going to do.”Asked if he still believes in Arsenal winning the title, his answer was simple …💬 “Of course.”Odegaard: ‘We weren’t sharp enough in front of goal’ Getty ImagesMartin Odegaard made a welcome return to the Arsenal starting XI but he wasn’t able to inspire his team-mates to a result in Manchester. Here is what the visitors’ captain said to Sky Sports after the match …💬 “Disappointed not to win. Obviously we wanted to come here and get a result, and I thought we were really up for it today. We played a good game, we pressed them really well, we had some really good moments. We looked a lot more dangerous in the second half and had a few big moments in front of goal.“Small margins to decide a game like this. We weren’t sharp enough in front of the goals and that’s why we go home with nothing.”More evidence of the big battle of the match You could put together a full gallery of images from the Haaland vs Gabriel battle this afternoon.In the blue corner ... Haaland was the winner!Erling Haaland has his say Getty ImagesThe match winner was pretty happy at full time and who can blame him — this is what he had to say when speaking to Sky Sports:💬 “I was quite happy. It was a great moment for me. It’s always like this, a lot of fighting and these kinds of things.“Every game is a final. When we are done speaking here, it is about recovering and getting ready for Burnley because that is as important as this win or the Chelsea game. “If I fell on the floor (in the challenge with Gabriel), which I will not do unless someone really attacks me, then it would be a red card. I haven’t seen the situation properly but it is what it is and I will not fall on the floor easily.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementThe winning goal Some finish from the ever-clinical Erling Haaland.He just knows how to find the back of the net from even the most difficult circumstances.Let’s hear from Bernardo Getty ImagesThe Manchester City midfielder scooped the player of the match award and it was easy to see why. Here’s how he reflected on that win, speaking to Sky Sports:💬 “Very big (win) … Two weeks ago this didn’t look very likely, this scenario. It was a tough game and a good game but we are happy we can be on the same points.“It was very good until we make a mistake and we changed the mood after the 20th minute. The second half was tough. It looked like we were in control of the game but they are always very dangerous. “They had two very big chances in a row and games are like this. The small details and the small margins make a difference. I’m really proud.”Another stunning Bernardo Silva performance With every passing Bernardo Silva performance, the knowledge he is leaving Manchester City at the end of the season must hurt more for fans. A modern club legend, he has served City so well in an amazing period of time under Pep Guardiola. Today was no different with so many touches on the ball and key interventions to stifle Arsenal. A game of the season contenderWhile that was almost certainly agony for both sets of fans, what a treat for the neutral as subscriber Jose A. says! Share your post-match thoughts on the discussion tab above. An opportunity missed This is an absolute headache for Arsenal, make no mistake about it. Mikel Arteta was on his knees after Kai Havertz’s missed chance late in the game.Arsenal’s players look wiped out and bereft at that loss. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFor a first time this season? The Athletic / Conor O’NeillAs for that Manchester City game in hand at Burnley on Wednesday, not only do they have the chance to draw level on points with Arsenal …As the graphic from Conor O’Neill shows, it could be the first time Manchester City finish a gameweek ahead of Arsenal in the Premier League table.And with it being mid April, which a time to do it. That was Oli Kay, reminding us all that some Manchester City supporters were handing out Arsenal branded bottles outside Etihad Stadium before kick-off. A fun skit that is going to make Arsenal fans wince a little harder now. For the record, I agree with him about today too. That was good afternoon where the post twice denied them in that second half.Arsenal did not bottle this performanceA huge win for Manchester City, who are now within three points of Arsenal with a game in hand. They can go top by beating Burnley on Wednesday night.Arsenal will wonder how this has happened from what looked like an unassailable position a month ago. I’ve been critical of their approach at times since the start of last season, but I really don’t think there’s much to criticise today — tactically, mentally, technically, physically, whatever. It was nothing like the Carabao Cup final defeat, which was really disappointing. They didn’t “bottle” it, as some will say.Haaland in the wars A ripped shirt, a face-off with Gabriel — Erling Haaland had a pretty physical battle today. He came away with the last laugh and the winning goal in the match, however.A handful from start to finish.Explaining why Gabriel avoided a red card Gabriel and Erling Haaland had been at each other all afternoon, with the Manchester City player gaining the upper hand when he won a physical duel to be first to the ball and put his side 2-1 ahead.Later in the second half the pair clashed again, with each having a firm hold on the other and Haaland losing a chunk of his undershirt in the process.Their third close encounter ended with them facing each other down — literally — and a yellow card apiece.Gabriel’s late flourish looked like a potential headbutt, but he was stepping away and there was no contact that would have looked like violent conduct to referee Anthony Taylor.VAR John Brooks would have been aware that his colleague had a good view of the incident and would have had scant evidence to justify recommending an upgrade to red.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFull-time stats zoneFascinating looking at the full-time numbers here. The possession levels remained similar from half-time, while Manchester City dominated territory in terms of touches in the opposition box.But Arsenal created some major chances in that second half — see their expected goals (XG) figure — and then either didn’t take them, or found the City defence (and also the post) in their way …FT: Manchester City 2-1 ArsenalPossession %: 59 — 41Shots: 15 — 9On target: 5 — 3XG: 1.41 — 1.53Big chances: 3 — 4Blocked shots: 5 — 3Touches in opposition box: 40 — 14 Duels won: 48 — 40Dispossessed: 10 — 6In short, they had the opportunities — and that might be why this defeat will hurt even more for Mikel Arteta. Party time for City fans The chase is on.Sun shining, beach ball out and in full voice, Manchester City fans celebrated that result with plenty of enthusiasm.I’m not quite sure it is warm enough to get your shirt off in Manchester just yet though!Was Gabriel lucky? If I can be controversial, I respected the decision not to send Gabriel off after the coming together with Haaland in the second half.So often we see overacting in response to minimal contact — both players were being aggressive in squaring up here. That said, Gabriel was pretty lucky to be able to see the game out given those are so often red cards. Consistency is key.Classic Haaland makes his markHow big a moment in the title race could that Erling Haaland goal be? It was an excellent quick release by Donnarumma, great work by O’Reilly to carry the ball forward, and then Haaland was so aggressive and single-minded in getting to the ball ahead of Gabriel. He had such a tough battle with Gabriel all afternoon. Gabriel was having the better of it until that point, but that was classic Haaland.O’Reilly becoming a genuine forceNico O'Reilly has quickly become the outstanding contender for England’s starting left-back at the World Cup with his recent performances.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Getty ImagesHard to ignore the gorgeous setting sun as the backdrop at Etihad Stadium. The smiles are beaming from Erling Haaland — golden locks finally free of his hair band and Gabriel — while Gianluigi Donnarumma has the widest grin, which probably includes a whole load of relief after his first-half error. For Mikel Arteta, this will hurt: his 10th defeat at the hands of Pep Guardiola. Getty ImagesThe Arsenal players head straight for the away fans, who applaud their efforts. They know it was close. And they know it is not over.FULL TIME: Manchester City victory! Getty ImagesFT: Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal The barrage of whistles from the stands is brutal — and finally, referee Anthony Taylor joins in.It’s over. Manchester City win the game and with it, have they just ripped Arsenal’s hands off the Premier League trophy?This is quite a finish, isn't it? Whatever happens here and for all the pre-match predictions about how this would go, I’m not sure many people expected this level of fight from Arsenal so deep into this match. They are making this a hell of a game late on.Wow. That was the moment for Arsenal. It’s an outstanding cross from Trossard and Havertz really should score with the header. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementHavertz misses a huge chance! Getty Images90+5’ Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal Outstanding defensive header at the far post from Matheus Nunes as Gabriel threatened Odegaard’s cross.And then … Wow!Trossard’s cross, Havertz flying header. And it flies millimetres over Donnarumma’s crossbar.So, so close. 90+3’ Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal I tell you what, if Arsenal do find an equaliser in the coming minutes here, we’re going to see a lot of that replay of Gabriel’s head against Haaland’s …The visitors are winding up some late pressure as I type.It’s not over yet90+1’ Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal Blimey. SEVEN added minutes to come.That feels like an awful lot more than I was expecting for no real major stoppages I can recall.Rodri calls time88’ Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal And now we have Rodri feeling an issue and calling to come off. Nico Gonzalez is on in his place as the Spaniard walks off.But it only comes after Savinho is introduced for Jeremy Doku.A real sense of time running out for Arsenal right now. Getty ImagesThe intensity of the battle between Haaland and Arsenal’s two centre-backs remains one of the most captivating parts of any meeting between these two teams.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementGyokeres, Foden into the action85’ Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal The only obvious reaction to all that is substitutions. Gyokeres is on, for Zumbimendi — so that is a proper attacking change.Cherki’s afternoon is done for Man City too. Phil Foden is on.Gabriel avoids red card after Haaland altercation Getty Images83’ Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal After a period of relative calm, it all kicks off — to the extent Erling Haaland’s hair is out of his hair band.A yellow card for Gabriel, who climbs on the striker’s back. Then has a little kick out. The two players then rut heads before Gabriel forces his head forward.In truth, there’s a couple of reds in that for me — but what do I know?Haaland is also booked, as is Pep Guardiola who I guess got to see the replays Bernardo remains a key influence Getty ImagesBernardo Silva ... Manchester City are gonna miss him, big time. I can’t forget that performance at Anfield in February when he dragged Manchester City back into a game that looked beyond them. It’s incredible he’s last man just now and winning a duel against Kai Havertz.Why is Khusanov still on the pitch?Just from an earlier moment in this second half while it was 1-1 … Anthony Taylor was quick to dismiss an appeal from Kai Havertz for a free kick — and with it a likely red card — when the Arsenal man went to ground under a challenge from Abdukodir Khusanov.The players were converging on the same space just outside the City box and their upper bodies clashed, but that would be written off by Taylor as a ‘coming together’ rather than a foul by the defender.Few such challenges are penalised in the Premier League, which places such an emphasis on allowing more physical contact. VAR John Brooks would have checked as a matter of routine, but would have endorsed Taylor’s view that there was nothing to see here.Further Arsenal changes74’ Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal Arsenal changes No 2 and 3, as Ben White and Leandro Trossard get involved.Cristhian Mosquera and Eberechi Eze are, unsurprisingly, the two players to be withdrawn. It all sounds a little tense inside the Etihad Stadium right now …SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementGabriel next to hit the post73’ Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal An Arsenal free kick is headed on goal by Gabriel at the far post. It hits O’Reilly’s side and then the post.Havertz finds a follow-up, but Donnarumma repels that from the floor.Another escape for the hosts.Arsenal unlucky — and at fault Getty ImagesThat City goal felt a bit tough on Arsenal on the back of those two near misses at the other end, when Havertz and Eze both came so close to scoring. But Arsenal’s right side was badly exposed in the lead up to Haaland scoring, enabling O’Reilly to carry the ball such a long way before feeding Doku and getting it back. Thereafter it’s about Haaland’s sheer desire to score.Fine margins here. Arsenal nearly find themselves in front, now find themselves behind. Mikel Arteta is deep in conversation with his assistants. How does he change it from here?Just as needed for Man City Getty ImagesI’d just written how City needed more from Semenyo and Haaland here … so listen, fair play!What I really like about that goal is Doku always knows he can trust O’Reilly’s touch to give him the ball in a tight space from a short distance, and have a good deal of belief that the youngster will be able to make something happen.Ripping the shirt off his back Getty Images67’ Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal Haaland held off Gabriel for the finish, which he enjoyed.Now the sleeve of Haaland’s undershirt is in tatters from another tussle with the Arsenal centre-back. Iconic images, these.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementGOAL: HAALAND SCORES! Getty Images65’ Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal HERE HE IS! Erling Haaland goes from anonymous to potential match-winner in a huge Premier League match.Beautiful snap for a run from Doku, who finds O’Reilly — and the cross is dispatched by Haaland at the far post because that’s what he does.Manchester City lead for a second time. Can they hold onto it a bit longer this time!?The luxury of Eze and OdegaardThat moment from Odegaard, setting up the shot from Eze, is something that Arsenal would have loved to have seen more of this season: two creative players with different profiles complementing each other nicely to create a chance. Even though that effort hit the post, those are the types of moments they need to continue looking for in the next half an hour.What a chance for Kai Havertz to put Arsenal in front — and then Eze hits the post! Arsenal are enjoying a good spell here. Yet again the momentum of the game has swung on an error in build-up.So close from Eze! Getty Images61’ Manchester City 1-1 Arsenal And now Eze is denied! It’s a stunning switch of feet and low curling left-footed shot from the Arsenal No 10, which strikes the base of the post and somehow squirms across the goal line without crossing it.Significant let-off for Manchester City, as Arsenal rediscover their ambition in this title clash. Donnarumma makes amends59’ Manchester City 1-1 Arsenal Redemption for Donnarumma! Huge save as Odegaard plays Havertz through on goal and the big Italian stands tall, blocking the effort superbly.That looked like being the lead for Arsenal. Havertz could not believe he was denied. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementArsenal holding firm Getty ImagesCity looking slightly out of ideas at the moment, let’s see if that carries on for long.Arsenal are defending those low balls into their box from wide positions very well, always there for a block.City forcing the issueWe’ve talked a lot about the Arsenal press but Manchester City are quick to pounce on any hesitation too. Khusanov robbed Eze in a dangerous area just now, presenting a chance for Doku. Eze has been a bit loose with his last couple of actions — a careless ball in the left channel moments earlier. Arsenal are finding it hard to retain the ball full stop at the moment.Havertz unhappy at Khusanov shove Getty Images53’ Manchester City 1-1 Arsenal Arsenal not seeing a lot of the ball since the restart, with the Manchester sun setting.But it’s much more about what you do with the ball when you do have it — and that Martinelli through ball is an utter peach to find Havertz’s run.The German is given a shove from Khusanov, which sends him to the ground. Referee Anthony Taylor waves away Arsenal appeals, including a perplexed Havertz. Martinelli not up to speedHaving said that about Martinelli, he’s had a really tough opening few minutes. He needs to realise the game he’s in, and quickly. This isn’t the time to be taking extra touches in your own box, as Donnarumma found out — and Raya almost did — in the first half.Off the post from Haaland! Getty Images50’ Manchester City 1-1 Arsenal Big chances from a corner as David Raya is put under major pressure beneath his own crossbar.His punch is limited, Khusanov’s shot is blocked and then Haaland rattles the outside of the post when it felt a certainty that the ball would nestle in the net.Arsenal survive, but it’s been a promising restart from the hosts. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMartinelli on the right may not be a common sight, but it has worked well for Arsenal on that side against Manchester City in particular recently. His equaliser against City at the Emirates came from a out-to-in run from the right wing, and he also started on that flank in Arsenal’s 5-1 win over Pep Guardiola’s side last season. Should the game become stretched as the teams search for a winner, he could be Arsenal’s trump card.Martinelli into the fray47’ Manchester City 1-1 Arsenal The halftime change belongs to Arsenal, and is no real surprise given Noni Madueke was a fitness doubt to feature at all today. Madueke makes way, with Gabriel Martinelli into the action. That’s a like for like replacement you imagine — or maybe not!Over to Art …SECOND HALF: Back underway46’ Manchester City 1-1 Arsenal The players are back out on the pitch, Bernardo Silva gets us going again — and there have been half-time changes in personnel too … Ice cold Cherki Getty ImagesAfter the dancing feet and the inch-perfect finish, staring down the supporters was an ice cold way to celebrate from Rayan Cherki. City's Mr Cool is in a blistering spell of form and is gifting Premier League spectators with one entertaining performance after another.I agree with Sam. It's the combination of the manner of the goal that City conceded – totally self-inflicted, in farcical circumstances – and how quickly that happened after Cherki's moment of brilliance. There wasn't even time for any Arsenal doubts to creep in, which they surely would have done had Donnarumma not made that blunder. Credit to Havertz, who has totally justified his inclusion ahead of Gyokeres, for pressing so aggressively. But it's an awful moment for Donnarumma.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementPhoto of the half Getty ImagesHow about this for a shot?Like some sort of modern footballing recreation of the evolution of man, Erling Haaland rises highest to meet a corner for City. Getty ImagesRayan Cherki reminds me so much of Anthony Edwards of the NBA’s Minnesota Timberwolves. The youthful exuberance of a young superstar, the brashness, showmanship, and indifference to tradition. And yet a player with such undeniable talent that it condemns fans who may take offence to his antics to just sit and enjoy the show. Quite the goal from the 22 year old that opened this match.The full range of emotions Getty ImagesHead in hands, arms outstretched, chin scratching befuddlement — it is all going on on the touchline for the two managers.Guardiola and Arteta are really feeling the full range of emotions about this match and I am not surprised. It has been jam packed with crazy moments to bring joy and frustrate those with partisan interest. Getty ImagesI know I've laboured this point by now but that Havertz goal really is a leveller in every sense, given the effect it's had on the emotions of the game. City had really capitalised on their pre-match confidence, relative to Arsenal's recent struggles, but the Donnarumma error sapped the energy out of the Etihad and it only started to return towards half-time. You feel like this can go either way at this point, quite possibly after another error in the build-up by either side. Half-time stats zoneHere is how the half-time numbers look. The hosts are dominating the ball and the final-third possession too. But one of those six dispossessions was more important than the other five …HT: Manchester City 1-1 ArsenalPossession %: 60 — 40Shots: 8 — 3On target: 2 — 1XG: 0.69 — 0.55Big chances: 2 — 1Blocked shots: 4 — 1Touches in opposition box: 15 — 6 Duels won: 29 — 21Dispossessed: 6 — 4On this occasion, the break might actually do Manchester City a favour — if they can get back to how they started the first half and catch Arsenal off-guard again. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Gabriel took a risk by leaning into the ball to block Rayan Cherki's shot just four minutes into the match. He was just about on the right side of the law because he was struck high on the arm, at the cut off point for a potential offence. And his lean was marginal, not extravagant.The incident was similar to a penalty awarded against James Tarkowski in the Leeds vs Everton game on the opening weekend of the season. But the ball struck the Everton defender much lower on the arm, and he threw his whole body into the line of the ball.I was impressed with the way Arsenal started that half. They were pressing man-to-man and following City's movements tightly. Guardiola has been trying to work those left-sided rotations with Doku inside and O'Reilly pushed on.You can find more insight from Liam and ask him tactics questions on the discussion tab a the top of this page.HALF-TIME: Fine margins and a few errors Getty ImagesHT: Manchester City 1-1 Arsenal And there it is. The half-time whistle.A part of me feared this was going to be a horrible cagey affair. It’s really not been that at all, and the work rate from both sides has been phenomenal.Level at the break.
